title: Stable channels support matrix and upgrade tooling proposal
creator: Maya Chen
description: Proposal to define a small set of long-lived release channels (Stable, Maintenance, Security-only) and a cross-product support matrix linking runtime, public API, SDK major lines, and console releases. Deliverables: 1) canonical channel definitions and support windows; 2) compatibility matrix and automatic compatibility checks for CI; 3) rollout gate spec (canary/percent/health checks/auto-rollback); 4) upgrade tooling plan (client SDK warnings, migration helpers, in-place schema checks, runtime shim layer). This ticket captures design decisions, risk trade-offs, implementation owners and a rollout timeline for Q2 2026.
acceptance_criteria: Channel definitions documented and published to Confluence
Support matrix completed and validated against current versions of runtime, API, SDKs and console
CI job that validates forward/backwards compatibility for runtime↔API added to release pipelines
Rollout gate library implemented with canary percentage controller and health thresholds
SDKs emit deprecation warnings and provide migration guides for breaking changes
Release playbook for customers and SEs with upgrade steps and rollback instructions
decision_record: 2025-11-12: Adopt three-channel model (Stable / Maintenance / Security-only) to limit cognitive load for customers
2026-01-21: Use semantic major boundary for breaking change windows; minor releases are compatible within channel
2026-02-05: Runtime will carry a channel tag (e.g., runtime-2.4-stable) and API will advertise minimum compatible runtime version
2026-02-28: Rollout gates will be policy-driven and pluggable; default policy uses 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% linear ramp with automated rollback on SLO breaches
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers pin to older runtime causing fragmentation. Mitigation: tooling to surface pinning and migration cost estimates via Console.
Risk: SDK churn across languages. Mitigation: require compatibility matrix entry for every SDK release and add deprecation metadata in package manifests.
Risk: CI false-positives blocking release. Mitigation: staged enforcement and opt-in flag for first two cycles, with human review required before hard block.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (Q1-Q2): Docs, compatibility matrix, CI checks, minimal rollout gate library
Phase 2 (Q2): SDK warning hooks and migration helpers; console UI for channel selection and upgrade recommendations
Phase 3 (Q3): Automated in-place upgrade tooling for Dedicated clusters and assisted migrations for Private customers
Key owners: Release infra (ENG-22311) implements CI checks; SDK teams implement warning hooks; Console team implements migration UI
testing_matrix: Unit tests for compatibility checkers across 3 most-used model sizes
Integration test: runtime-2.x <-> api-1.x cross-version traffic for read/write paths
E2E smoke: canary rollout triggers alert, rollback verified by automated job
Load test: ensure batching/kv-cache behavior unaffected by channel metadata
rollout_gates_spec: Gate types: canary (percent), canary (host-based), staged-by-region, feature-flagged fallback
Health signals: token latency p50/p95, error rate, request queue growth, model quality regression alerted via evals harness
Rollback conditions: sustained SLO breach for 3 minutes OR error rate > 2% for 5 minutes
Automation: controller evaluates metrics every 30s, implements percent changes and can trigger rollbacks
customer_communication: Pre-announcement: 60 days before channel maintenance windows are enforced
Migration guides: step-by-step instructions per SDK and runtime, with automated runnable samples
Console: inline upgrade cost estimate and impact assessment for pinned customers
Support: dedicated migration office hours and runbook for high-risk enterprise customers
